evidence.text: The 工 headword calls the graph pictographic and proposes a carpenter’s square, a tool for drawing right angles or squares, as its referent. It describes a late-Shang reduction of an early one-ended box to a horizontal stroke and reports thicker lower strokes in earlier Western Zhou bronze forms before a thinner horizontal became standard. It proposes semantic uses including craft worker, skilled or skillful, engineering, achievement later written 功, and official or service roles. This is the author’s account, not a settled identification or chronology.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析, 工 entry, graph analysis and examples, lines 122–128
evidence.text: The database describes oracle and bronze forms as a tool, reporting competing identifications: a bladed tool whose upper part may have served a carpenter’s-square function (attributed to 季旭昇), a carpenter’s square (楊樹達), or a building tool (鄒景衡、劉新民). It cites oracle-bone uses as a state/place name, status or occupation, and a whole-graph loan for 貢; bronze examples include an official title, 工師 and uses for 功, with a Warring States slip example read as 功. The entry does not date each cited artifact, and these examples alone do not establish a complete semantic chain.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transmitted 說文解字 工 entry and 段玉裁注
evidence.field: 卷五, 工部, entry and commentary
evidence.text: The transmitted entry glosses 工 as 巧飾, explains the form as a person having 規榘, compares it with 巫, and records 𢒄 as 古文工从彡. Duan Yucai relates 巧飾 to skilled finishing and extends it to doing something well. This historical lexicographic account differs from modern tool-identification proposals; it does not prove the graph’s pictured referent or specify the direction/type of the 𢒄–工 relationship.
evidence.title: 說文解字「工」

evidence.source: 邓飞, “商代‘宗工’名称考”, 西南大学汉语言文献研究所; originally 《考古与文物》, 2011年第5期
evidence.field: Discussion of oracle-bone uses of 工 and 百工, especially lines 244–308
evidence.text: The author reviews contrasting readings of oracle-bone 工 as official/官 and argues that the occurrences show differing social positions; examples include 丧工, 执工, 多工, and 百工. He cautions against treating every oracle-bone use as simply an official title and interprets some 多工/百工 uses as makers of fine handicrafts. He also notes that Zhou 百工 contexts vary in institutional status. This supports retaining distinctions among title/status and craft-worker uses rather than merging them into one sense.
evidence.title: 商代“宗工”名称考

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, Taiwan Ministry of Education, 2024 version 7
evidence.field: 工 entry, modern and historical definition sections, lines 54–78
evidence.text: The dictionary lists senses for 工 including refined/skillful, skilled worker, official, musician, skill, being skilled, laboring activity, construction, industrial abbreviation, and a verb/nominal equivalent of 功. It supplies both classical quotations and unmarked modern examples such as 木工、矿工、水電工 for the worker sense and 工整 for refined/skillful. The entry does not mark these current examples obsolete, supporting present usage for those senses while leaving their semantic chronology unresolved.
evidence.title: [A01148] 工 - 教育部《異體字字典》
